_schema_notes.coverage: Authoritative schema for all DID formats — DD Form 1664 (pre-2014) and free-text (post-2014 MIL-STD-963C)
_schema_notes.did_format: Set to 'dd_form_1664' or 'free_text'. Determines which fields are expected to be populated.
_schema_notes.963c_compliant: True if the DID was prepared under MIL-STD-963C (2014 or later). False for older DIDs.
_schema_notes.reserved_fields: Fields marked RESERVED are present in one format but not the other. Always include them — set to empty string or empty array when not applicable.
_schema_notes.preparation_instructions: Official MIL-STD-963C name for what was previously called 'requirements'. Contains the numbered sections of the DID. All section numbers are normalized to strictly numeric dot-notation (1, 1.1, 1.1.1). Letter-based source numbering (2.a, 3.1.b) is converted to numeric equivalents (2.1, 3.1.2).
_schema_notes.asterisk: True if the requirement number is followed by * in the source document (conditional requirement).

title: Software Bill of Materials (SBOM)
summary: Defines the format, content, and intended use of a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) that documents software components, supply chain relationships, and cybersecurity-related data for a DoD system or application.
use_relationship:
The Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) provides information that defines the software components for a particular system. The details of the SBOM include Cybersecurity and Integration related data and documents a record of the details and supply chain relationships of the elements that comprise a software baseline for a specific Department of Defense (DoD) product, component, system, or application.  The cognizance and knowledge of the key software elements that are installed on any DoD system, equipment or device aids with timely risk analysis, vulnerability management and remediation associated with the instance and/or use of software applications, libraries, source code and executables.  The SBOM Data Item Description (DID) references the mission related concerns and their integration within the system's software, firmware and supporting development libraries of source code and executables.  Software obsolescence is a part of the DoD Program Manager's Total System Life Cycle Management responsibilities.

A current and accurate SBOM for DoD systems enables System and Manufacturing/Production Engineers, logisticians and software developers the ease of identifying and isolating software components that pose imminent cybersecurity threats, malicious intent or compromised system operations.  Potential negative impact to a system's cybersecurity posture can be thwarted with regular SBOM review.

This Data Item Description (DID) contains the format, content, and intended use of information for the data product resulting from the work task described by the contract, where a corresponding SBOM for each program phase is defined.
distribution_statement: DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT A: Approved for public release; distribution is unlimited.

preparation_instructions.title: Format
preparation_instructions.content: Field Name, Definition, Notes, Data Type (see Table 1)

preparation_instructions.title: Content
preparation_instructions.content: The SBOM shall contain all information specified below.  Fields which do not require data shall be left blank. Below contains a glossary of terms provided for the field content entries followed by the Format in Table 1 and an example in Table 2.

children.title: Supplier
children.content: This is the name of the supplier or software originator.

children.title: Supplier Point of Contact
children.content: This is the contact information for the supplier point of contact to include organization, email, and phone number.

children.title: Supplier Cage Code(s)
children.content: This is the CAGE code that has been assigned to the supplier by Defense Logistics Agency (DLA).

children.title: Software Type
children.content: This describes whether the software is Commercial Off the Shelf (COTS), Government Off the Shelf (GOTS) or Supplier Proprietary Developed.

children.title: Software Use
children.content: This describes the software end use within the system such as Application Interface (API), Library, Compiler, Tool, Software as a Service (SaaS), Firmware, or Operating System.

children.title: Free and Open Source
children.content: This is a flag to signify whether this software is (FOSS)

children.title: Software Name
children.content: This is the formal name of the software.

children.title: Component/Application Identifier
children.content: This is the equipment component or module that the software resides in.

children.title: Unique Identifiers
children.content: This is the software version designator or the logical reference to software build version update.

children.title: Dependency relationship
children.content: This specifies the software required for component operation.

children.title: Hash Function
children.content: This is the hash function with specificity.

children.title: Previous SW Version
children.content: This is the software transition/build-up to arrive at this version.

children.title: Licensing Restrictions
children.content: This identifies if there are any restrictions levied on the license. The specific restrictions are not included.

children.title: Licensing Expiration
children.content: This is the expiration date for the license.

children.title: Uniformity implementation
children.content: This is the description of how the software is uniformly applied and date when implemented.

children.title: SBOM Product Owner / Custodian
children.content: This is the contact information for the authority for the software product.

children.title: Date stamp
children.content: This is the date for the SBOM at the time of program phase delivery.

children.title: Program Phase
children.content: This is the program phase for which this SBOM applies based on DoD Acquisition Pathways.

preparation_instructions.title: Media Requirement
preparation_instructions.content: The SBOM shall be in an electronic format that supports auto generation and machine readability, and it is based on formats such as SPDX and CycloneDX.

preparation_instructions.title: Other considerations
preparation_instructions.content: this Data Item Description formally documents the actively maintained software and enables the awareness of currently supported software applications.
